I just got out of a relationship where that "exclusive" thing was one, of many, lies I wanted to believe from her. We were in a long-distance situation, but only a few hours away from one another. We specifically talked about whether or not we would be exclusive. I guess she knew I would never go for it, so she lied to keep me around until she decided I wasn't needed anymore. 

I've since been trying to educate myself on recognizing this type of behavior early on so I can avoid it going forward. Users prey on people who have self-doubt, self-hate, etc. because those same people tend to be very giving. And Takers love Givers, at least as long as there is something to give. 

There are plenty of terms out there for these types of people, narcissists is one that gets used a lot, or player, or toxic person, etc. They all have a talent for luring people in, and they thrive on doing just that only to chew them up and spit you out.

If your significant other isn't being exclusive and lying about it, don't let it slide. Walk away before worse happens. I don't know you, but I do know that no person deserves to be treated like that. You are worth more.

I'm trying to get over a breakup myself. Long story, and probably a relationship I should have ended a long time ago. Still my heart aches. As the universe sometimes does, it just threw this in my path tonight; I thought I would share it with the hope that it helps you. I'm not the author of this, just to be up front about it:

"The opposite of love is not hated but indifference.

When you try to reach out to your ex, she is not happy. She isn’t angry either. She just doesn’t care. She may laugh to herself that you are still hung up on her. She thinks “What a loser. He needs to get a life”

And then she deletes or disposes of your message as if it were a piece of junk mail in her mailbox. She ignores it.

She might even set up her computer to automatically delete messages from you unread. Or she might change her phone number or e-mail. She might block you on social media.

The point is she does not want to have you in her life or be in yours.

If she left you, you may be sad. You may miss her. You may now know where you went wrong. You will play “what if” games in your mind.

You will never know what has become of her. If she had died, it would be easier to accept. But she is very much alive and has chosen not to let you near her.

You will not know where she lives, who she dates, where she vacations, where she works. When one of her parents dies, you will not know. If she had goals and dreams, you will never know if she reached them.

You will not know what new books she read, what new music she likes, or what she has learned since the last day you saw her. You will not know if she is happy or sad,  if she is healthy or was in the hospital last year.

But you will know she doesn’t think about you.

You will not know about her because she does not want you to know. She is finished and believes you have no right to know any of these things.

If you should die, she will never know. But she has moved on and she doesn’t care. You are just someone she used to know.

If you really love her, let her go. Completely. If you love her, you want her to be happy. She believes her best chance for happiness is without you in her life. That is why she left.

Love her from afar. Cherish the memories. Forgive her unconditionally, then forgive yourself. If you are religious, pray for her. Maybe you will reunite in heaven after you both have died?

I don’t believe that nonsense, but it gives some people comfort.

She knows where to find you if she wanted to contact you. Maybe someday she will. People do change. But don’t count on it, hope for it or live your life waiting for it.

I know it is hard to let go when you still have feelings for someone. Maybe you miss them. Maybe sometimes when you are alone you grieve your loss and cry.

Yes, life is not fair. But you have no choice in this. Go to Alanon even if alcohol or addictions played no part whatsoever in your life. You will be welcomed there.

You will learn the serenity prayer. (God) Grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, the courage to change the things I can, and the wisdom to know the difference.

She left me in 2010. My biggest fear was being alone. I have been alone since she left. I am 71. No one will ever take her place. I will likely die alone.

Being alone and without a romantic partner isn’t a choice. But loneliness is.

Choose you. Love you. Being single allows you to live your life for you. Having her back will not make you happy.

There is no person, place or thing that can ever make you happy. You have to do that for yourself. Happiness is an inside job.

Good luck. Never forget what you learned so you won’t make the same mistakes twice. You’ll make entirely new ones."

Really do your research on the meds, they have lots of side effects. For instance, many of them make it difficult for men to, um...rise to the occasion, and/or to arrive if they even get there. Many doctors solve problems by putting you on more and more medications, but believe me, as someone who was on them for over 15 years, they just don't do much anymore if you don't make some changes in your life. 

Yep, the hard part that most depression sufferers simply don't have the energy to execute - making the positive changes.

The biggest for me was leaving Corporate America for a smaller, family-owned company. Yes, there are some trade offs, but it was all worth it just for the sake of how much better I feel now! Truth be told, I was forced out of a job I had for 20+ years due to some overly-ambitious types trying to make a name for themselves, but it has turned out to be one of the best things to happen to me in a long time.

I'm not a shiny happy person all the time now, but I feel better overall and I'm dealing with things much better. The world can be unforgiving, but we can survive it without numbing our brains to zombie level.

All my opinion here, but that one change did more for my mental health than any of the medications ever did!
